title: Chard and mushroom hash with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food: potatoes, onion, mushrooms, garlic, chard, eggs, butter, oil and simple seasonings.

supermarket.reason: Every item is an everyday mainstream supermarket buy, and chard is in season in November.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan and a lidded frying pan, and boiling, frying and cooking eggs under a lid suits a confident beginner.

works.reason: Parboiling 700g of potatoes before frying, adding the chard stalks before the leaves and steaming four eggs under a lid gives a sensible, well-seasoned hash for four.

honest_times.reason: Dicing and slicing plus turning the hash fits roughly 25 active minutes, and the boiling and covered egg time roughly matches the 20 minutes printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, including salt in the cooking water, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot potato and chard hash suits a mid-November morning, and 300g of chard, stalks and leaves, makes it central rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English instructions a neighbour would give.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potatoes, vegetables and an egg each make a filling, wholesome breakfast a family would happily repeat.
